sentences.en: We have one cardinal rule on 99% Invisible.
sentences.zh: 我们在“99%隐形”有一条核心准则。

sentences.en: No cardinals, meaning we don't deal with the natural world, only the built world.
sentences.zh: 没有自然物，也就是说我们不探讨自然世界，只探讨人造世界。

sentences.en: So when I read John Mwellum's brilliant book called Wild Ones,
sentences.zh: 所以当我读到约翰·穆勒姆的出色著作《荒野之民》时——

sentences.en: a sometimes dismaying, weirdly reassuring story about looking at people looking at animals in America,
sentences.zh: 这是一本有时令人沮丧、却又奇异地带有抚慰色彩的书，讲述了观察美国人观察动物的故事——

sentences.en: I didn't think I'd ever do an episode of 99% Invisible about it, I just read it for fun.
sentences.zh: 我本来没想过要为此做一期“99%隐形”的节目，我只是读着玩罢了。

sentences.en: But then I saw John perform stories from the book live with musical accompaniment,
sentences.zh: 但后来我看到约翰现场表演书中的故事，还有音乐伴奏，

sentences.en: and I thought, I need to put this on the radio.
sentences.zh: 我觉得，我得把这个搬上电台。
我还是习惯把这叫作电台。

sentences.en: Anyway, what you need to know about Wild Ones is that it isn't a book about nature.
sentences.zh: 总之，关于《荒野之民》，你需要知道的是，它并不是一本关于自然的书。

sentences.en: It's a book about how we fit nature into our modern lives.
sentences.zh: 它是一本关于我们如何将自然融入现代生活的书。

sentences.en: Wild Ones is about the cutesy stuffed animals, the eco tours,
sentences.zh: 《荒野之民》讲的是那些可爱的毛绒玩具、生态旅游，

sentences.en: and the Byzantine methods of conservation that evolve
sentences.zh: 以及当我们的野生动物体验从自然之物变成设计之物时，

sentences.en: when our experience with wildlife goes from something natural to something designed.
sentences.zh: 所演变出的繁复错综的保护方法。

sentences.en: Human-animal interaction has become a designed experience,
sentences.zh: 人与动物的互动已经变成了一种被设计的体验，

sentences.en: and the story of that transition, as the title of the book suggests,
sentences.zh: 而正如书名所示，这种转变的故事

sentences.en: is sometimes dismaying, and also weirdly reassuring.
sentences.zh: 有时令人沮丧，却也奇异地令人安心。

sentences.en: John Mwellum is friends with the band Black Prairie,
sentences.zh: 约翰·穆勒姆和“黑色草原”乐队是朋友，

sentences.en: and as he was writing the book,
sentences.zh: 正当他在写这本书的时候，

sentences.en: they concocted this idea of the band creating a soundtrack to the book,
sentences.zh: 他们萌生了一个想法，由乐队为这本书创作一张原声带，

sentences.en: and the result was an extended EP called Wild Ones,
sentences.zh: 结果就诞生了一张名为《荒野之民》的加长版EP，

sentences.en: a musical score for the things you might see in your head
sentences.zh: 这是一支配乐，对应着你在脑海中可能会浮现出的画面——

sentences.en: when you reflect on certain characters and incidents that you read in the book.
sentences.zh: 当你回想起书中读到的某些人物和事件时。

sentences.en: The writer and the band then went on a short tour
sentences.zh: 于是这位作家和乐队进行了一次短途巡演，

sentences.en: with the song and story extravaganza that I'm going to play for you today.
sentences.zh: 带着我今天要给大家播放的这场歌曲与故事的视听盛宴。

sentences.en: When I saw them perform this live in San Francisco,
sentences.zh: 当我在旧金山看他们现场演出时，

sentences.en: I freaked out, it was so good,
sentences.zh: 我简直惊呆了，太精彩了，

sentences.en: and I accosted them in the dressing room and said,
sentences.zh: 我在后台休息室缠着他们说：

sentences.en: you have to let me share this with my audience.
sentences.zh: 你们一定要让我把这个分享给我的听众。

sentences.en: So here it is, and here we go.
sentences.zh: 所以这就是它，我们开始吧。
被称为菱斑海龟的小海龟，

sentences.en: skitter out of the water around JFK Airport in New York,
sentences.zh: 从纽约肯尼迪机场周围的水域里匆忙爬出，

sentences.en: They're heading for a patch of sand where they like to lay their eggs,
sentences.zh: 它们正朝着一小片沙滩走去，那是它们喜欢产卵的地方，

sentences.en: and they have to cross over one of the airport's runways to get there,
sentences.zh: 而要在到达那里前穿过机场的一条跑道，

sentences.en: Sometimes there's so many turtles on the move at once
sentences.zh: 有时同时移动的海龟数量实在太多，

sentences.en: that the control tower has to delay flights.
sentences.zh: 以至于控制塔台不得不延误航班。

sentences.en: Now the press loves doing stories about how funny this is,
sentences.zh: 现在媒体很喜欢报道这有多么滑稽，

sentences.en: how a fleet of giant airplanes can be held up by just a few tiny turtles.
sentences.zh: 庞大的飞机机队竟然会被区区几只小海龟给难住。

sentences.en: But hold that picture in your mind and think about the Caribbean Sea in 1492.
sentences.zh: 但请在脑海中保留这个画面，想想1492年的加勒比海。

sentences.en: There were almost a billion sea turtles living in it back then.
sentences.zh: 当时那里生活着近十亿只海龟。

sentences.en: Columbus' men, anchored in the Caribbean,
sentences.zh: 哥伦布的手下在加勒比海抛锚停泊时，

sentences.en: wrote about being kept awake at night
sentences.zh: 在文字记录中提到他们夜不能寐，

sentences.en: by the thwacking of so many turtle shells against the sides of their ship.
sentences.zh: 因为无数的龟壳不断撞击着船舷，发出砰砰的声响。

sentences.en: Notice how that scene is the exact opposite of the scene at JFK.
sentences.zh: 注意，那个场景跟肯尼迪机场的场景完全相反。

sentences.en: It's not a fleet of giant airplanes being held up by a few tiny turtles.
sentences.zh: 不是庞大的飞机机队被几只小海龟难住。

sentences.en: It's a giant fleet of turtles bombarding just a few relatively tiny ships.
sentences.zh: 而是一个庞大的海龟舰队在对区区几艘相对渺小的船只发起狂轰滥炸。

sentences.en: So I wrote this book about people and wild animals in America,
sentences.zh: 所以我写了这本关于美国人和野生动物的书，

sentences.en: and it only really started because I wanted to show my daughter
sentences.zh: 而这一切的起因其实只是因为我想带我女儿

sentences.en: endangered species in the wild before they disappeared.
sentences.zh: 去看野外的濒危物种，在它们消失以前。

sentences.en: Like a lot of people, I think, I felt this pang.
sentences.zh: 我想和很多人一样，我感到了这种隐痛。

sentences.en: I knew that all around us, beautiful parts of the world are expiring.
sentences.zh: 我知道在我们周围，世界上美丽的部分正在消亡。

sentences.en: And I also knew that people in the future, they might not even notice.
sentences.zh: 我也知道未来的人们，他们甚至可能都不会注意到。

sentences.en: For them, a world without whales or wilderness might feel normal.
sentences.zh: 对他们来说，一个没有鲸鱼或荒野的世界可能会感觉很正常。

sentences.en: I wanted to counteract that forgetting that's bound to take hold over time.
sentences.zh: 我想要对抗这种随着时间推移必然会占据上风的遗忘。

sentences.en: Scientists call it shifting baseline syndrome.
sentences.zh: 科学家称之为“基线偏移综合征”。

sentences.en: It means that all of us accept the version of the world we inherit as normal.
sentences.zh: 这意味着我们所有人都将继承的世界版本视为理所当然的正常状态。

sentences.en: Over the years, we watch forests get logged or animals disappear,
sentences.zh: 这些年来，我们看着森林被砍伐或动物消失，

sentences.en: but when the next generation comes along,
sentences.zh: 但当下一代人成长起来时，

sentences.en: they accept that depleted version of nature as their normal.
sentences.zh: 他们就把那种日渐贫瘠的自然状态当作了他们的正常。

sentences.en: It's hard to zoom out, really feel the changes
sentences.zh: 很难跳脱出来，去真正真切感受到那些

sentences.en: that are stacking up across the generations.
sentences.zh: 在代际之间不断叠加的变化。

sentences.en: I can't even imagine what an ocean filled with a billion sea turtles must feel like.
sentences.zh: 我甚至无法想象，一片挤满十亿只海龟的海洋会是什么感觉。

sentences.en: Last winter, I was in Hawaii, and I saw three sea turtles,
sentences.zh: 去年冬天我在夏威夷看到了三只海龟，

sentences.en: and I flipped the f*** out.
sentences.zh: 我整个人激动得都快疯了。

sentences.en: I felt like I was in Eden.
sentences.zh: 我觉得自己仿佛置身伊甸园。

sentences.en: It wasn't so long ago, though, that America was a kind of Eden,
sentences.zh: 不过没过多久以前，美利坚还曾是一处伊甸园般的所在，

sentences.en: when people could be dwarfed and engulfed by wild animals
sentences.zh: 那时的人们会被野生动物所包围并显得无比渺小，

sentences.en: in a way that feels almost impossible now.
sentences.zh: 那种感觉在如今看来几乎是不可能的。

sentences.en: In the late 1800s, trains would sometimes have to stop for four or five hours
sentences.zh: 在19世纪后期，火车有时不得不停驶四五个小时，

sentences.en: as streams of buffalo moved across the tracks.
sentences.zh: 因为成群的水牛正从铁轨上横穿而过。

sentences.en: Occasionally, a stampede would batter into the side of a train, derailing it.
sentences.zh: 偶尔，一场惊慌狂奔会猛烈撞击火车侧面，导致其脱轨。

sentences.en: A witness described one of these scenes, 1871 in Kansas.
sentences.zh: 一位目击者描述了其中一个场景，那是1871年的堪萨斯州。

sentences.en: Each individual of buffalo went at it with the desperation and despair
sentences.zh: 每一头水牛都带着一种绝望与疯狂的神情，

sentences.en: of plunging against green locomotive cars.
sentences.zh: 朝着沉重的火车车厢直冲猛撞。

sentences.en: Just as blind madness chanced and directed,
sentences.zh: 正如盲目的疯狂所偶然导致和驱使的那样，

sentences.en: after having trains thrown off the track twice in one week,
sentences.zh: 在经历了一周内两次火车被撞翻出轨之后，

sentences.en: conductors learned to have a very decided respect
sentences.zh: 列车员们学会了对水牛的种种怪脾气

sentences.en: for the idiosyncrasies of the buffalo.
sentences.zh: 保持一种极其敬畏的态度。

sentences.en: This man's name was William Temple Hornaday.
sentences.zh: 这个人名叫威廉·坦普尔·霍纳代。

sentences.en: He was a bombastic Midwesterner with an elaborate mustache.
sentences.zh: 他是个留着精心修剪的胡子、言语夸张的中西部人。

sentences.en: Hornaday was head taxidermist at the Smithsonian,
sentences.zh: 霍纳代是史密森尼学会的首席剥制师，

sentences.en: and he traveled the globe, hunting exotic animals
sentences.zh: 他曾游历全球，猎捕珍禽异兽

sentences.en: and stuffing them for the museum.
sentences.zh: 并将它们做成标本供博物馆展出。

sentences.en: In India, after he took down an elephant,
sentences.zh: 在印度，当他击倒一头大象后，

sentences.en: he climbed atop the carcass and popped open a bass ale.
sentences.zh: 他爬到动物尸体顶上，砰地打开了一瓶淡艾尔啤酒。

sentences.en: Once, he trapped an orangutan, named it Little Man,
sentences.zh: 有一次，他捉到一只红毛猩猩，给它起名叫“小不点”，

sentences.en: and gave it to Andrew Carnegie as a pet.
sentences.zh: 并把它作为宠物送给了安德ルー·卡耐基。

sentences.en: It sounds weird, but for Hornaday,
sentences.zh: 这听起来很奇怪，但对霍纳代来说，

sentences.en: killing these animals was a kind of conservation.
sentences.zh: 杀死这些动物其实是一种保护。
他坚信通过把它们制成标本，
他就是在为未来的子孙后代保存濒危物种，

sentences.en: for the future generations that might not know them
sentences.zh: 以免这些动物灭绝后，后人连它们长什么样都不知道。
通过动物剥制术，他可以使它们永生。

sentences.en: Through taxidermy, he could make them immortal.
sentences.zh: 通过动物剥制术，他可以使它们永生。

sentences.en: and saw that Americans were killing so many buffalo so rapidly
sentences.zh: 发现美国人杀害水牛的速度如此之快、数量如此之多，

sentences.en: that the prairie was almost empty.
sentences.zh: 以至于大草原几乎空无一物。

sentences.en: He figured there were maybe less than 300 buffalo left in the wild.
sentences.zh: 他估计野外剩下的水牛可能还不到300只。

sentences.en: And so he did what he thought was the most helpful and logical thing.
sentences.zh: 于是他做了他认为最有用、最合逻辑的事。

sentences.en: He lit out for Montana to kill several dozen of them.
sentences.zh: 他动身前往蒙大拿州去猎杀几十只水牛。
霍纳代在蒙大拿州射杀了25只水牛，

sentences.en: and he built the best-looking ones into an exhibit at the museum.
sentences.zh: 并把其中长得最好看的那些做成标本摆在博物馆里展出。

sentences.en: He gathered them around a fake watering hole, looking for Lorne.
sentences.zh: 他把它们围在一个假水坑周围，做出寻望远方的样子。

sentences.en: But from there, his thinking evolved.
sentences.zh: 但从那时起，他的思想发生了转变。

sentences.en: He realized he was basically just a funeral director,
sentences.zh: 他意识到自己基本上只是个殡仪馆馆长，

sentences.en: embalming the species that America was exterminating.
sentences.zh: 在为美国正在灭绝的物种进行防腐处理。

sentences.en: What if we actually tried to keep these animals alive?
sentences.zh: 如果我们真的试着让这些动物活下来会怎么样？

sentences.en: And so he became one of America's first real wildlife conservationists,
sentences.zh: 于是他成为了美国最早的真正的野生动物保护主义者之一，

sentences.en: an activist, a lobbyist, a celebrity.
sentences.zh: 一位活动家、说客和名人。

sentences.en: America was killing every conceivable kind of animal in their way,
sentences.zh: 美国人当时正在赶尽杀绝挡路的各种可以想象的动物，

sentences.en: and Hornaday stood up for all of them,
sentences.zh: 而霍纳代挺身而出捍卫了它们所有者，
从灰熊这样的标志性动物

sentences.en: to lowlier, less majestic things like the squirrel.
sentences.zh: 到松鼠这种较为卑微、没那么雄伟的生物。

sentences.en: A live squirrel in a tree is poetry in motion.
sentences.zh: 树上一只活生生的松鼠就是运动中的诗篇。

sentences.en: We ask every American to lend a hand to save the silver tail.
sentences.zh: 我们请求每一位美国人伸出援手，拯救银尾松鼠。

sentences.en: There was really only one animal on the continent
sentences.zh: 大陆上其实只有一种动物
是霍纳代不怎么担心的。

sentences.en: It would seem too mighty to be brought down by men with guns,
sentences.zh: 它显得过于强大，不可能被拿着枪的人类击倒，

sentences.en: and it lived in a cold and brutal wilderness
sentences.zh: 而且它生活在寒冷而残酷的荒野中，

sentences.en: that men couldn't possibly take over.
sentences.zh: 那是人类绝对无法接管的。

sentences.en: The polar bear is the king of the frozen north!
sentences.zh: 北极熊是冰冷北方之王！

sentences.en: It's not very probable that the polar bear
will ever be exterminated by man.

sentences.zh: 这是霍纳代在1914年写下的文字。

sentences.en: Back then, no one could have imagined a problem
sentences.zh: 在当时，没有人能想象出像气候变化

sentences.en: But think about how quickly climate change
sentences.zh: 但想想气候变化的速度有多快，

sentences.en: has changed the polar bear's reputation in our minds.
sentences.zh: 它已经改变了我们在心目中对北极熊的看法。
它已经从嗜血的食人杀手
变成了脆弱的溺水受害者。

sentences.en: 200 years ago, Arctic explorers wrote about polar bears
sentences.zh: 200年前，北极探险家在文字中写到北极熊

sentences.en: leaping into their boats and trying to eat them,
sentences.zh: 会跳进他们的船里并试图吃掉他们，

sentences.en: even if they lit the bear on fire.
sentences.zh: 哪怕他们把北极熊点燃也无济于事。

sentences.en: But recently, when I went to the tiny northern town
sentences.zh: 但最近，当我来到那个自称为

sentences.en: that calls itself the polar bear capital of the world,
sentences.zh: 世界北极熊之都的小镇时，

sentences.en: Martha Stewart had just arrived to film the animals
sentences.zh: 玛莎·斯图尔特刚刚抵达，准备拍摄这些动物

sentences.en: for her daytime show on the Hallmark Channel.
sentences.zh: 用于她在霍尔马克频道的日间节目。

sentences.en: The town is called Churchill, Manitoba.
sentences.zh: 这个镇子叫曼尼托巴省的丘吉尔镇。

sentences.en: It's on the edge of Hudson Bay,
sentences.zh: 它位于哈得逊湾的边缘，

sentences.en: and every fall, right before the bay freezes over,
sentences.zh: 每年秋天，就在海湾结冰之前，

sentences.en: Churchill gets overrun with about 900 polar bears
sentences.zh: 丘吉尔镇就会涌入大约900只北极熊
和10000名来看北极熊的游客。
熊经常漫步游荡进小镇。

sentences.en: They like hanging out at the elementary school, especially.
sentences.zh: 它们特别喜欢在小学附近闲逛。

sentences.en: and a squad of bear patrol officers
will come chase the animals back onto the tundra
Bears that won't budge are tranquilized
sentences.zh: 不肯挪动的熊会被麻醉

sentences.en: and shipped out to a Quonset hut near the airport.
sentences.zh: 并运送到机场附近的一个科朗斯铁皮屋里。

sentences.en: Once this so-called polar bear jail fills up,
sentences.zh: 一旦这个所谓的北极熊监狱装满，
每只动物就会再次被注射麻醉药，

sentences.en: and airlifted one at a time
to an area north of town.
Crowds of tourists come out to watch these bear lifts,
sentences.zh: 成群的游客涌来观看这些熊的空运，

sentences.en: and I went to one myself.
There was something just a little ceremonial
sentences.zh: 我去看的那次熊的空运

sentences.en: about the bear lift I went to,
sentences.zh: 透着那么一点点仪式感，
身穿制服的野生动物官员

sentences.en: on a net at the center of the crowd,
sentences.zh: 安放在人群中央的网兜上，
他们小心翼翼地把它的爪子

sentences.en: to show how far out of our way
it's a breathtaking thing to watch,

sentences.zh: 是一件令人叹为观止的事。

sentences.en: the edges of the net lifted.

sentences.zh: 收缩成了一个 U 形，

sentences.zh: 但我们现在帮助动物的方式
已经演变成了一种超现实的
持续了 20 世纪 70 年代的大部分时间。
随时间推移而改变的底线。

来到威斯康星州的乡村，
近一百年来的数量还要多。

sentences.en: And in the years to come,
By the end of his life,

sentences.zh: 简直是个无可救药的笨蛋。
开始朝另一个方向移动，
更多美感而非更少美的方向，
再次想象一下肯尼迪机场的那幕场景，
关闭引擎、减速降落的情景，

好让这个海龟的微小族群
